overview.text: The female, or ovarian, reproductive system functions to produce gametes and reproductive hormones, just like the male reproductive system; however, it also has the additional task of supporting the developing fetus and delivering it to the outside world.
overview.label: 27.2 Anatomy and Physiology of the Ovarian Reproductive System

overview.text: The ovaries are located within the pelvic cavity, and are supported by the mesovarium, an extension of the peritoneum that connects the ovaries to the broad ligament.
overview.label: 27.2 Ovaries

overview.text: The bladder lies anterior to the uterus in females, posterior to the pubic bone and anterior to the rectum.
overview.label: 25.2 Bladder

ovaries.text: Paired ovals, they are each about 2 to 3 cm in length, about the size of an almond.
ovaries.label: 27.2 Ovaries

ovaries.text: The ovaries are located within the pelvic cavity, and are supported by the mesovarium, an extension of the peritoneum that connects the ovaries to the broad ligament.
ovaries.label: 27.2 Ovaries

ovaries.text: Finally, the ovary itself is attached to the uterus via the ovarian ligament.
ovaries.label: 27.2 Ovaries

ovaries.text: Beneath the tunica albuginea is the cortex, or outer portion, of the organ.
ovaries.label: 27.2 Ovaries

tubes.text: Each of the two uterine tubes is close to, but not directly connected to, the ovary and divided into sections.
tubes.label: 27.2 The Uterine Tubes

tubes.text: The uterine tubes also have three layers: an outer serosa, a middle smooth muscle layer, and an inner mucosal layer.
tubes.label: 27.2 The Uterine Tubes

isthmus.text: The isthmus is the narrow medial end of each uterine tube that is connected to the uterus.
isthmus.label: 27.2 The Uterine Tubes

isthmus.text: Each of the two uterine tubes is close to, but not directly connected to, the ovary and divided into sections.
isthmus.label: 27.2 The Uterine Tubes

infundibulum.text: The wide distal infundibulum flares out with slender, finger-like projections called fimbriae.
infundibulum.label: 27.2 The Uterine Tubes

infundibulum.text: The nearby uterine tube, either left or right, receives the oocyte.
infundibulum.label: 27.2 The Uterine Tubes

ampulla.text: The middle region of the tube, called the ampulla, is where fertilization often occurs.
ampulla.label: 27.2 The Uterine Tubes

ampulla.text: Each of the two uterine tubes is close to, but not directly connected to, the ovary and divided into sections.
ampulla.label: 27.2 The Uterine Tubes

uterus.text: Its average size is approximately 5 cm wide by 7 cm long (approximately 2 in by 3 in) when a female is not pregnant.
uterus.label: 27.2 The Uterus and Cervix

uterus.text: The portion of the uterus superior to the opening of the uterine tubes is called the fundus.
uterus.label: 27.2 The Uterus and Cervix

uterus.text: The middle section of the uterus is called the body of uterus (or corpus).
uterus.label: 27.2 The Uterus and Cervix

fundus.text: The portion of the uterus superior to the opening of the uterine tubes is called the fundus.
fundus.label: 27.2 The Uterus and Cervix

body.text: The middle section of the uterus is called the body of uterus (or corpus).
body.label: 27.2 The Uterus and Cervix

wall.text: The wall of the uterus is made up of three layers.
wall.label: 27.2 The Uterus and Cervix

wall.text: The most superficial layer is the serous membrane, or perimetrium, which consists of epithelial tissue that covers the exterior portion of the uterus.
wall.label: 27.2 The Uterus and Cervix

wall.text: The middle layer, or myometrium, is a thick layer of smooth muscle responsible for uterine contractions.
wall.label: 27.2 The Uterus and Cervix

cervix.text: The cervix is the narrow inferior portion of the uterus that projects into the vagina.
cervix.label: 27.2 The Uterus and Cervix

cervix.text: The cervix produces mucus secretions that become thin and stringy under the influence of high systemic plasma estrogen concentrations, and these secretions can facilitate sperm movement through the reproductive tract.
cervix.label: 27.2 The Uterus and Cervix

vessels.text: In the luteal phase of the menstrual cycle, special branches off of the uterine artery called spiral arteries supply the thickened stratum functionalis.
vessels.label: 27.2 The Uterus and Cervix

bladder.text: The bladder lies anterior to the uterus in females, posterior to the pubic bone and anterior to the rectum.
bladder.label: 25.2 Bladder

bladder.text: The bladder is a retroperitoneal organ whose "dome" distends superiorly when the bladder is filling with urine.
bladder.label: 25.2 Bladder

passage.text: Following ovulation, the secondary oocyte surrounded by a few granulosa cells is released into the peritoneal cavity.
passage.label: 27.2 The Uterine Tubes

passage.text: The nearby uterine tube, either left or right, receives the oocyte.

passage.text: Once inside, the muscular contractions and beating cilia move the oocyte slowly toward the uterus.
passage.label: 27.2 The Uterine Tubes

passage.text: If the oocyte is successfully fertilized, the resulting zygote will begin to divide into two cells, then four, and so on, as it makes its way through the uterine tube and into the uterus.

notes: 3D models: Human Reference Atlas (HuBMAP), made from the Visible Human Female (National Library of Medicine). The donor was 59 years old (NLM). OpenStax gives sizes for adults in general.

HRA's metadata for the uterus model says it was made from the Visible Human Male. A uterus cannot come from a male body, so this looks like an error in the metadata; the model sits in the female body with the other female organs. Flagged for review.
OpenStax's current edition calls this the ovarian reproductive system (section 27.2).

Size: in this model the uterus with the cervix measures 6.3 by 5.2 cm along its two longest axes, and the ovaries are 2.5 cm (left) and 2.6 cm (right) long. OpenStax 27.2 gives about 5 by 7 cm for a uterus that is not pregnant, and 2 to 3 cm for each ovary.
